sanskrit: sa tvaṃ nivṛttabandhas tu nivṛttaś cāpi karmataḥ sarvavit sarvajit siddho bhava bhāvavivarjitaḥ
english: And so you, having turned away from bondage and turned away likewise from action, become one who knows all, conquers all, and is perfected — wholly free of clinging to existence.

sanskrit: saṃyamena navaṃ bandhaṃ nivartya tapaso balāt saṃprāptā bahavaḥ siddhim apy abādhāṃ sukhodayām
english: By self-restraint and through the power of austerity, having warded off any new bondage, many have attained perfection — unhindered and dawning into bliss.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca aśokaṃ śokanāśārthaṃ śāstraṃ śāntikaraṃ śivam niśamya labhate buddhiṃ tāṃ labdhvā sukham edhate
english: Nārada said: There is a sorrowless teaching, made to destroy sorrow, peace-bestowing and benign; hearing it, one gains wisdom, and gaining that wisdom one flourishes in happiness.

sanskrit: śokasthānasahasrāṇi bhayasthānaśatāni ca divase divase mūḍham āviśanti na paṇḍitam
english: Thousands of occasions for grief and hundreds of occasions for fear, day after day, beset the fool — but never the wise.

sanskrit: tasmād aniṣṭanāśārtham itihāsaṃ nibodha me tiṣṭhate ced vaśe buddhir labhate śokanāśanam
english: Therefore, for the destruction of all that is unwelcome, mark well this ancient tale of mine; if the mind is held under control, it attains the undoing of sorrow.

sanskrit: aniṣṭasaṃprayogāc ca viprayogāt priyasya ca manuṣyā mānasair duḥkhair yujyante alpabuddhayaḥ
english: From union with what is unwelcome and from separation from what is dear, men of meager understanding are yoked to the sufferings of the mind.

sanskrit: dravyeṣu samatīteṣu ye guṇās tān na cintayet tān anādriyamāṇasya snehabandhaḥ pramucyate
english: When possessions have passed away, one should not dwell upon the merits they had; for him who ceases to prize them, the bond of affection is loosed.

sanskrit: doṣadarśī bhavet tatra yatra rāgaḥ pravartate aniṣṭavad dhitaṃ paśyet tathā kṣipraṃ virajyate
english: Wherever passion arises, there one should become a discerner of faults; one should regard even what is cherished as if unwelcome, and so quickly grow dispassionate.

sanskrit: nārtho na dharmo na yaśo yo 'tītam anuśocati apy abhāvena yujyeta tac cāsya na nivartate
english: He who grieves over what is past gains thereby no profit, no merit, no renown; he may even be brought to ruin, and yet the lost thing does not return to him.

sanskrit: guṇair bhūtāni yujyante viyujyante tathaiva ca sarvāṇi naitad ekasya śokasthānaṃ hi vidyate
english: By the strands of nature all beings are joined together, and just so are they parted; this is no ground for the grief of any single one.

sanskrit: mṛtaṃ vā yadi vā naṣṭaṃ yo 'tītam anuśocati duḥkhena labhate duḥkhaṃ dvāv anarthau prapadyate
english: He who grieves over the past — whether one dead or one lost — gains only sorrow upon sorrow, and falls into a twofold misfortune.

sanskrit: nāśru kurvanti ye buddhyā dṛṣṭvā lokeṣu saṃtatim samyak prapaśyataḥ sarvaṃ nāśrukarmopapadyate
english: Those who, beholding through wisdom the unbroken succession in the worlds, shed no tears — for one who sees all things rightly, no occasion for weeping arises.

sanskrit: duḥkhopaghāte śārīre mānase vāpy upasthite yasmin na śakyate kartuṃ yatnas tan nānucintayet
english: When an affliction of suffering befalls, whether of the body or of the mind, and nothing can be done against it, one should not brood upon it.

sanskrit: bhaiṣajyam etad duḥkhasya yad etan nānucintayet cintyamānaṃ hi na vyeti bhūyaś cāpi pravardhate
english: This is the medicine for sorrow: that one should not dwell upon it; for sorrow brooded over does not depart, but rather grows the greater.

sanskrit: prajñayā mānasaṃ duḥkhaṃ hanyāc chārīram auṣadhaiḥ etad vijñānasāmarthyaṃ na bālaiḥ samatām iyāt
english: Mental suffering one should slay with wisdom, and bodily suffering with remedies; this is the power of discernment — let him not sink to the level of the foolish.

sanskrit: anityaṃ yauvanaṃ rūpaṃ jīvitaṃ dravyasaṃcayaḥ ārogyaṃ priyasaṃvāso gṛdhyet tatra na paṇḍitaḥ
english: Youth, beauty, life, the hoarding of wealth, health, the company of loved ones — all are impermanent; in these the wise man does not grasp with greed.

sanskrit: na jānapadikaṃ duḥkham ekaḥ śocitum arhati aśocan pratikurvīta yadi paśyed upakramam
english: A man ought not, by himself alone, to grieve over a calamity that has befallen a whole land; without grieving he should act against it, if he sees a course of remedy.

sanskrit: sukhād bahutaraṃ duḥkhaṃ jīvite nātra saṃśayaḥ snigdhatvaṃ cendriyārtheṣu mohān maraṇam apriyam
english: In life there is far more suffering than happiness — of this there is no doubt; through delusion comes attachment to the objects of sense, and death is held unwelcome.

sanskrit: parityajati yo duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ vāpy ubhayaṃ naraḥ abhyeti brahma so 'tyantaṃ na taṃ śocanti paṇḍitāḥ
english: The man who utterly renounces both pain and pleasure alike attains absolutely to Brahman; for him the wise do not grieve.

sanskrit: duḥkham arthā hi tyajyante pālane na ca te sukhāḥ duḥkhena cādhigamyante nāśam eṣāṃ na cintayet
english: Riches are won with pain and given up with pain; in their keeping there is no happiness, and with pain are they gained — at their loss one should not grieve.

sanskrit: anyām anyāṃ dhanāvasthāṃ prāpya vaiśeṣikīṃ narāḥ atṛptā yānti vidhvaṃsaṃ saṃtoṣaṃ yānti paṇḍitāḥ
english: Attaining one greater state of wealth after another, men remain unsatisfied and go to their destruction; the wise, however, attain contentment.

sanskrit: sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitam
english: All hoards end in depletion, all risings end in falling, all unions end in separation, and life itself ends in death.

sanskrit: anto nāsti pipāsāyās tuṣṭis tu paramaṃ sukham tasmāt saṃtoṣam eveha dhanaṃ paśyanti paṇḍitāḥ
english: There is no end to thirst, but contentment is the supreme happiness; therefore the wise look upon contentment itself as wealth in this world.

sanskrit: nimeṣamātram api hi vayo gacchan na tiṣṭhati svaśarīreṣv anityeṣu nityaṃ kim anucintayet
english: Not even for the space of an eyeblink does the passing of one's years stand still; when one's own body is impermanent, why brood as though anything were eternal?

sanskrit: bhūteṣv abhāvaṃ saṃcintya ye buddhvā tamasaḥ param na śocanti gatādhvānaḥ paśyantaḥ paramāṃ gatim
english: Reflecting on the non-being inherent in all beings, those who have come to know what lies beyond darkness do not grieve; their journey is accomplished, and they behold the supreme goal.

sanskrit: saṃcinvānakam evainaṃ kāmānām avitṛptakam vyāghraḥ paśum ivāsādya mṛtyur ādāya gacchati
english: This man, still gathering and never sated in his desires — death, falling upon him as a tiger upon its prey, seizes him and is gone.

sanskrit: athāpy upāyaṃ saṃpaśyed duḥkhasya parimokṣaṇe aśocann ārabhetaiva yuktaś cāvyasanī bhavet
english: Yet should one see a means for the release from suffering, without grieving he should set to work upon it, steadfast and free of vice.

sanskrit: śabde sparśe ca rūpe ca gandheṣu ca raseṣu ca nopabhogāt paraṃ kiṃ cid dhanino vādhanasya vā
english: In sound, in touch, in form, in smells, and in tastes, there is nothing more than their enjoyment — for the rich man or the poor alike.

sanskrit: prāk saṃprayogād bhūtānāṃ nāsti duḥkham anāmayam viprayogāt tu sarvasya na śocet prakṛtisthitaḥ
english: Before beings come together there is no suffering, but only well-being; at the separation of all things, however, let him not grieve who abides in his own nature.

sanskrit: dhṛtyā śiśnodaraṃ rakṣet pāṇipādaṃ ca cakṣuṣā cakṣuḥśrotre ca manasā mano vācaṃ ca vidyayā
english: By firmness one should guard the loins and the belly, the hands and the feet by the eye, the eye and the ear by the mind, the mind by speech, and speech by knowledge.

sanskrit: praṇayaṃ pratisaṃhṛtya saṃstuteṣv itareṣu ca vicared asamunnaddhaḥ sa sukhī sa ca paṇḍitaḥ
english: Withdrawing affection from both the familiar and the stranger, he who moves through the world unpuffed by pride — he is happy, and he is wise.

sanskrit: adhyātmaratir āsīno nirapekṣo nirāmiṣaḥ ātmanaiva sahāyena yaś caret sa sukhī bhavet
english: Seated and rejoicing in the inner Self, free of expectation, free of craving, he who goes through the world with the Self alone for his companion becomes happy.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca sukhaduḥkhaviparyāso yadā samupapadyate nainaṃ prajñā sunītaṃ vā trāyate nāpi pauruṣam
english: Nārada said: When the reversal of happiness and sorrow comes to pass, neither wisdom, nor sound policy, nor manly effort can save a man from it.

sanskrit: svabhāvād yatnam ātiṣṭhed yatnavān nāvasīdati jarāmaraṇarogebhyaḥ priyam ātmānam uddharet
english: By his very nature a man should persist in effort, for the diligent man does not sink down; from old age, death, and disease he should rescue the self that is dear to him.

sanskrit: rujanti hi śarīrāṇi rogāḥ śārīramānasāḥ sāyakā iva tīkṣṇāgrāḥ prayuktā dṛḍhadhanvibhiḥ
english: For diseases, of the body and of the mind, torment the bodies of men like sharp-pointed arrows loosed by mighty bowmen.

sanskrit: vyādhitasya vivitsābhis trasyato jīvitaiṣiṇaḥ avaśasya vināśāya śarīram apakṛṣyate
english: The body of the sick man — anxious in his cravings, trembling, longing to live yet helpless — is dragged away to its destruction.

sanskrit: sravanti na nivartante srotāṃsi saritām iva āyur ādāya martyānāṃ rātryahāni punaḥ punaḥ
english: The nights and days flow on and never return, like the currents of rivers, bearing away the lifespan of mortals again and again.

sanskrit: vyatyayo hy ayam atyantaṃ pakṣayoḥ śuklakṛṣṇayoḥ jātaṃ martyaṃ jarayati nimeṣaṃ nāvatiṣṭhate
english: This unceasing alternation of the bright and the dark fortnights ages the mortal who is born, and does not pause even for the blink of an eye.

sanskrit: sukhaduḥkhāni bhūtānām ajaro jarayann asau ādityo hy astam abhyeti punaḥ punar udeti ca
english: That sun, ageless yet aging the joys and sorrows of beings, goes down to its setting and rises again, again and again.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvān ādāya bhāvān apariśaṅkitān iṣṭāniṣṭān manuṣyāṇām astaṃ gacchanti rātrayaḥ
english: Taking up the never-before-seen, unsuspected conditions of men — the welcome and the unwelcome alike — the nights pass on to their setting.

sanskrit: yo yam icched yathākāmaṃ kāmānāṃ tat tad āpnuyāt yadi syān na parādhīnaṃ puruṣasya kriyāphalam
english: Whatever a man might wish, according to his desire, that very thing among objects of longing he would attain — if only the fruit of a man's action were not subject to another power.

sanskrit: saṃyatāś ca hi dakṣāś ca matimantaś ca mānavāḥ dṛśyante niṣphalāḥ santaḥ prahīṇāś ca svakarmabhiḥ
english: For men who are self-controlled, capable, and wise are seen to come to nothing, deprived of the fruit of their own labors.

sanskrit: apare bāliśāḥ santo nirguṇāḥ puruṣādhamāḥ āśīrbhir apy asaṃyuktā dṛśyante sarvakāminaḥ
english: While others, foolish, devoid of merit, the basest of men, though joined to no blessings, are seen to have every desire fulfilled.

sanskrit: bhūtānām aparaḥ kaś cid dhiṃsāyāṃ satatotthitaḥ vañcanāyāṃ ca lokasya sa sukheṣv eva jīryate
english: Yet another, ever bent upon doing harm to creatures and upon deceiving the world, grows old amid nothing but pleasures.

sanskrit: aceṣṭamānam āsīnaṃ śrīḥ kaṃ cid upatiṣṭhati kaś cit karmānusṛtyānyo na prāpyam adhigacchati
english: Upon one man, idle and sitting still, Fortune comes to wait; while another, for all his pursuit of action, does not attain what he seeks.

sanskrit: aparādhaṃ samācakṣva puruṣasya svabhāvataḥ śukram anyatra saṃbhūtaṃ punar anyatra gacchati
english: Declare, then, what the fault of a man is, given his own nature: the seed conceived in one place goes again to another.

sanskrit: tasya yonau prasaktasya garbho bhavati vā na vā āmrapuṣpopamā yasya nivṛttir upalabhyate
english: When that seed has lodged in the womb, an embryo may form or may not; its failure to develop is found to be like the falling of the mango's blossom.

sanskrit: keṣāṃ cit putrakāmānām anusaṃtānam icchatām siddhau prayatamānānāṃ naivāṇḍam upajāyate
english: For some who long for sons, who desire continuance of their line and strive with all their power for success, no fertile seed comes to be at all.

sanskrit: garbhāc codvijamānānāṃ kruddhād āśīviṣād iva āyuṣmāñ jāyate putraḥ kathaṃ pretaḥ pitaiva saḥ
english: And for those who recoil from offspring as from an enraged venomous serpent, a long-lived son is nonetheless born — how is it that the father himself becomes, in him, but a ghost made manifest?

sanskrit: devān iṣṭvā tapas taptvā kṛpaṇaiḥ putragṛddhibhiḥ daśa māsān paridhṛtā jāyante kulapāṃsanāḥ
english: Having worshipped the gods and performed austerities, by wretched men greedy for sons, and borne in the womb ten months — there are born defilers of the family.

sanskrit: apare dhanadhānyāni bhogāṃś ca pitṛsaṃcitān vipulān abhijāyante labdhās tair eva maṅgalaiḥ
english: Others are born to wealth and grain and enjoyments amassed by their fathers in abundance, obtained through those very auspicious rites.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ samabhipretya maithunasya samāgame upadrava ivāviṣṭo yoniṃ garbhaḥ prapadyate
english: When two come together, drawn to one another in the union of intercourse, the embryo enters the womb as though it were a calamity taking possession.

sanskrit: śīrṇaṃ paraśarīreṇa nicchavīkaṃ śarīriṇam prāṇināṃ prāṇasaṃrodhe māṃsaśleṣmaviceṣṭitam
english: Worn away within another's body, stripped of its skin, the embodied thing — amid the obstruction of the living creature's breath, a stirring of flesh and phlegm —

sanskrit: nirdagdhaṃ paradehena paradehaṃ calācalam vinaśyantaṃ vināśānte nāvi nāvam ivāhitam
english: scorched by another's body, itself a wavering further body, perishing at the term of its perishing, like one boat made fast to another.

sanskrit: saṃgatyā jaṭhare nyastaṃ retobindum acetanam kena yatnena jīvantaṃ garbhaṃ tvam iha paśyasi
english: A drop of seed, lifeless, set by chance within the belly — by what striving do you behold it here as a living embryo?

sanskrit: annapānāni jīryante yatra bhakṣāś ca bhakṣitāḥ tasminn evodare garbhaḥ kiṃ nānnam iva jīryate
english: In that very belly where food and drink are digested and what is eaten is consumed — why is the embryo not digested like food?

sanskrit: garbhamūtrapurīṣāṇāṃ svabhāvaniyatā gatiḥ dhāraṇe vā visarge vā na kartur vidyate vaśaḥ
english: The course of the embryo, of urine, and of excrement is fixed by their own nature; in their retention or their release, the agent has no power.

sanskrit: sravanti hy udarād garbhā jāyamānās tathāpare āgamena sahānyeṣāṃ vināśa upapadyate
english: For some embryos flow out from the belly even as they are being born; and of others the destruction comes about along with their very coming-to-be.

sanskrit: etasmād yonisaṃbandhād yo jīvan parimucyate prajāṃ ca labhate kāṃ cit punar dvaṃdveṣu majjati
english: He who escapes alive from this entanglement of the womb, and gains some offspring, sinks once more into the play of opposites.

sanskrit: śatasya sahajātasya saptamīṃ daśamīṃ daśām prāpnuvanti tataḥ pañca na bhavanti śatāyuṣaḥ
english: Of a hundred born together, some reach the seventieth and some the hundredth stage of life — yet of these, five do not attain a hundred years.

sanskrit: nābhyutthāne manuṣyāṇāṃ yogāḥ syur nātra saṃśayaḥ vyādhibhiś ca vimathyante vyālaiḥ kṣudramṛgā iva
english: There are, beyond doubt, no fixed means by which men may rise up again; they are churned and crushed by diseases, as small beasts by serpents.

sanskrit: vyādhibhir bhakṣyamāṇānāṃ tyajatāṃ vipulaṃ dhanam vedanāṃ nāpakarṣanti yatamānāś cikitsakāḥ
english: For those devoured by diseases, who give up vast wealth, the physicians, for all their striving, cannot draw off the pain.

sanskrit: te cāpi nipuṇā vaidyāḥ kuśalāḥ saṃbhṛtauṣadhāḥ vyādhibhiḥ parikṛṣyante mṛgā vyādhair ivārditāḥ
english: And even those skilled physicians, expert and well-stocked with remedies, are themselves dragged off by diseases, like deer harried by hunters.

sanskrit: te pibantaḥ kaṣāyāṃś ca sarpīṃṣi vividhāni ca dṛśyante jarayā bhagnā nāgā nāgair ivottamaiḥ
english: They too, drinking decoctions and clarified butters of many kinds, are seen broken by old age, like elephants overthrown by mightier elephants.

sanskrit: ke vā bhuvi cikitsante rogārtān mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ śvāpadāni daridrāṃś ca prāyo nārtā bhavanti te
english: And who on earth tends the beasts and birds afflicted by disease, the wild creatures and the destitute? Yet for the most part they are not so tormented.

sanskrit: ghorān api durādharṣān nṛpatīn ugratejasaḥ ākramya roga ādatte paśūn paśupaco yathā
english: Even kings, terrible, unassailable, and of fierce splendor, disease overpowers and carries off, as a herdsman takes his cattle.

sanskrit: iti lokam anākrandaṃ mohaśokapariplutam srotasā sahasā kṣiptaṃ hriyamāṇaṃ balīyasā
english: So is this world, none coming to its aid, overwhelmed by delusion and grief, hurled all at once into the current and swept away by that mightier force.

sanskrit: na dhanena na rājyena nogreṇa tapasā tathā svabhāvā vyativartante ye niyuktāḥ śarīriṣu
english: Not by wealth, nor by kingdom, nor by fierce austerity, do those innate natures, appointed to embodied beings, ever be set aside.

sanskrit: na mriyeran na jīryeran sarve syuḥ sarvakāmikāḥ nāpriyaṃ pratipaśyeyur utthānasya phalaṃ prati
english: They would not die, they would not grow old, all would have every desire fulfilled, and none would meet with anything unwelcome as the fruit of their striving — were it otherwise.

sanskrit: upary upari lokasya sarvo bhavitum icchati yatate ca yathāśakti na ca tad vartate tathā
english: Higher and ever higher above the world each man wishes to be, and strives to the limit of his power — and yet it does not come to pass so.

sanskrit: aiśvaryamadamattāṃś ca mattān madyamadena ca apramattāḥ śaṭhāḥ krūrā vikrāntāḥ paryupāsate
english: And upon men drunk with the intoxication of power, and drunk with the intoxication of liquor, the vigilant, the crafty, the cruel, the bold dance attendance — biding their time.

sanskrit: kleśāḥ pratinivartante keṣāṃ cid asamīkṣitāḥ svaṃ svaṃ ca punar anyeṣāṃ na kiṃ cid abhigamyate
english: For some, troubles turn back unforeseen of their own accord; while for others, strive as they will, nothing whatever is attained.

sanskrit: mahac ca phalavaiṣamyaṃ dṛśyate karmasaṃdhiṣu vahanti śibikām anye yānty anye śibikāgatāḥ
english: And a great disparity of reward is seen in the conjunctions of action: some bear the palanquin, while others ride within it.

sanskrit: sarveṣām ṛddhikāmānām anye rathapuraḥsarāḥ manujāś ca śatastrīkāḥ śataśo vidhavāḥ striyaḥ
english: Though all alike long for prosperity, some go forth with chariots leading the way; and there are men with a hundred wives, and women widowed by the hundred.

sanskrit: dvaṃdvārāmeṣu bhūteṣu gacchanty ekaikaśo narāḥ idam anyat paraṃ paśya mātra mohaṃ kariṣyasi
english: Among beings that take their delight in the pairs of opposites, men go their way one by one, each alone; behold now this other, higher truth — do not give yourself over to delusion.

sanskrit: tyaja dharmam adharmaṃ ca ubhe satyānṛte tyaja ubhe satyānṛte tyaktvā yena tyajasi taṃ tyaja
english: Renounce both righteousness and unrighteousness, renounce both truth and falsehood; and having renounced both truth and falsehood, renounce that by which you renounce.

sanskrit: etat te paramaṃ guhyam ākhyātam ṛṣisattama yena devāḥ parityajya martyalokaṃ divaṃ gatāḥ
english: This supreme secret has been declared to you, O best of seers — that by which the gods, abandoning the world of mortals, went to heaven.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā śukaḥ paramabuddhimān saṃcintya manasā dhīro niścayaṃ nādhyagacchata
english: Bhīṣma said: Having heard the words of Nārada, Śuka, supreme in wisdom and steadfast, pondered them in his mind, yet could not arrive at a settled resolve.

sanskrit: putradārair mahān kleśo vidyāmnāye mahāñ śramaḥ kiṃ nu syāc chāśvataṃ sthānam alpakleśaṃ mahodayam
english: "In sons and wives there is great affliction, in the recitation of sacred lore great toil — what then might be the everlasting abode, of little affliction and great fruition?"

sanskrit: tato muhūrtaṃ saṃcintya niścitāṃ gatim ātmanaḥ parāvarajño dharmasya parāṃ naiḥśreyasīṃ gatim
english: Then, pondering for a moment, he who knew the higher and the lower of righteousness fixed upon the goal determined for himself — the supreme path that leads to highest beatitude.
